learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of the kinematic and dynamic behavior of a rigid body, the theory of machines and mechanisms.

Have the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems of rigid body kinematics and dynamics and simple mechanisms and machines using established methods.
Have the ability to design and conduct experiments in machine and mechanism theory, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Possess technical and laboratory competencies in machine and mechanism theory.
Have the ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems of rigid body kinematics and dynamics, simple mechanisms and machines.
Have the ability to combine theory and practice to solve problems of rigid body kinematics and dynamics, simple mechanisms and machines.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in machine and mechanism theory and their limitations.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and perform experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by means of the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and perform experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Mechanics. Statics. Point Kinematics. Unit systems
The particle and the rigid body
Orthonormal Bases dependent on a scalar
Motion of a Rigid Body with a fixed point
Motion of a Rigid Body with a fixed axis
Determination of velocities in mechanism members
Determination of accelerations in mechanism members
Relationship of accelerations and velocities of kinematic pair points
Work and Energy in Planar Mechanisms
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 must be obtained in each part of the final exam (EF1 > 4 and EF2 > 4). The final grade calculation depends on the results of continuous assessment (EC1 and EC2). If both continuous assessments are passed (>5/10), the final grade is calculated as 0.1*Practices + 0.45*EC1 + 0.45*EC2. If only one continuous assessment is passed, the formula adjusts to include the corresponding final exam part. If neither continuous assessment is passed, the final grade is 0.1*Practices + 0.15*EC1 + 0.15*EC2 + 0.3*EF1 + 0.3*EF2. In the extraordinary call, students who followed continuous assessment will have it considered, or they can opt for a 100% final exam if more favorable, with the same minimum final exam score requirement.
